trust_decision.summary: The `version` argument of MCP tool `set_functype_version` must be an allowlisted package specifier, because the string is interpolated into `functype@<version>` and executed by `execFileSync("pnpm", ["add", spec])`, after which the just-installed package is dynamic-imported; the decision is made in the tool handler before the spec is built, plus a registration gate (tool not exposed over HTTP) and a loopback default for the HTTP listener.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the MCP tool `set_functype_version`, so a reader opens its addTool block first and finds the spec built as `functype@` plus the raw argument and fed straight to `pnpm add` with no validation.

fix_sites.entry_point: MCP tool `set_functype_version` (execute handler: isSafeFunctypeVersion allowlist plus `--ignore-scripts`)

server startup / createServer(): the addTool call is wrapped in `if (exposeSetVersion)` with exposeSetVersion = !isHttpTransport(); the instructions/toolList at packages/mcp-server/src/index.ts:25-34 are built from the same flag
HTTP transport bootstrap in main(): HOST default changed from 0.0.0.0 to 127.0.0.1
published CLI entry `functype-mcp-server --help` (HOST default text, plus the new tools line)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the transport posture is a separate deployment concern: TRANSPORT_TYPE already defaults to stdio in the wrapper (bin.ts:5-7, README:110), so validating `version` in the handler closes the reported RCE and the HTTP gate plus the HOST default can be left alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The tool advertises dist-tags (`latest`) and range prefixes (`^0.45.0`) in its own parameter description, so an over-broad strict-semver check (or a blanket ban on non-exact versions) breaks the documented legitimate inputs.

O6_input_shapes: dist-tags (latest, next, beta, alpha, canary, rc)
rejected alias syntaxes (file:/tmp/evil, npm:evil@1.0.0, git+https://..., https://....tgz, github:attacker/evil)
rejected separators/identity changes (embedded @, ../, backslash Windows paths, '/')
rejected whitespace/control chars (leading/trailing space, newline, '1.4.4 || file:/evil')
rejected empty / non-version garbage / shell metacharacters

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An env-var/CLI-driven version pin that runs `pnpm add functype@$FUNCTYPE_VERSION` and then re-imports `functype/cli` before serving.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: data.ts already owns the install-then-dynamic-import sequence (`require.resolve("functype/cli")` followed by a cache-busted import), so a maintainer adding reproducible version pinning for CI would extend this loader rather than the tool handler, and would not go through the new regex.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second specifier source consumed at bootstrap, e.g. `FUNCTYPE_PKG`, a registry override, or a tarball path read next to TRANSPORT_TYPE/HOST/PORT and handed to the same install path.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: main() already reads the whole deployment config from env and the fix's transport gate lives there, so a companion env knob for the package spec looks natural in that block.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Extending `validate_code` module resolution so non-`functype/*` or subpath specifiers are loaded from the installed dist dir chosen by user-supplied text.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: resolveModuleNames already special-cases `functype` and `functype/*` and reads files from a resolved dist directory, so a maintainer widening supported imports would touch exactly here.

O9_family: CWE-829 inclusion of functionality from an untrusted control sphere - package-manager alias/specifier injection into `pnpm add` leading to attacker package install and dynamic-import code execution

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm 11.8 workspace monorepo + turbo; ts-builds (tsdown build, vitest, eslint, prettier); tsx for scripts
O10_build.project_tests: packages/mcp-server/test/docs.spec.ts (docs data loader) and packages/mcp-server/test/validate.spec.ts (TS type-check of snippets), run with vitest via `pnpm -F functype-mcp-server test`; no test exists for set_functype_version at the pinned commit (the fix adds test/security.spec.ts).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Blocklist the obvious alias prefixes - reject the version if it contains a colon or starts with file:/npm:/git+/http - and pass everything else to the `functype@` spec.

out_of_scope_notes: `validate_code` is reachable unauthenticated over httpStream and its resolver accepts arbitrary import specifiers from user code (packages/mcp-server/src/lib/validator/compiler-host.ts:90-108), letting the compiler host read files outside the package; that is a different sink from the package-install RCE and was not pursued.
After the fix the HTTP listener still has no authentication; binding publicly is a documented explicit opt-in (`HOST=0.0.0.0` plus fronting auth), noted only, not pursued.
unverified: Repository size in MB (no shell available in this session), so the `tiny_repo` red flag could be neither confirmed nor excluded; the packages tree alone holds 553 source/doc files and there is a separate Astro docs site.
Whether the hidden behavioural tests exercise a real `pnpm add` (which needs a registry) or only the exported `isSafeFunctypeVersion` / tool registry; only the latter can run fully offline.

Whether `pnpm add --ignore-scripts` can still install a legitimate published functype version whose published tarball would need lifecycle scripts (packages/functype/package.json defines no install/postinstall/prepare script at the pinned commit, so no evidence of breakage).
